record.field: Head of Engineering at Ethara.AI — an AI-data company building human-in-the-loop datasets for training, aligning and evaluating LLMs (math, code, reasoning). Runs engineering end-to-end: inherits ~25 engineers, expected to reach ~45 within 12 months; Gurugram, on-site. Owns the engineering roadmap, architecture for shipped systems, and engineering hiring; proposes budget; co-owns research-to-production handoff with the CTO.

ROLE CALIBRATION — Head of Engineering (engineering leadership, NOT an ML-research role).
Year-one mandate the hire must credibly own (anchor competence claims against these three problems): 1. Ship a production-grade internal EVALUATION PLATFORM: 10K+ eval tasks/day across hundreds of concurrent projects; multi-turn, tool-use and agentic evals (not just single-turn scoring); dataset versioning and lineage that survives client audits; integration with client-side model endpoints (OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Vertex, on-prem). 2. Scale the ANNOTATION PLATFORM ~3x in volume WITHOUT linear cost scaling: latency targets (P95 task latency), annotator-productivity telemetry with real-time quality signals, role-based data-governance controls at SOC 2 Type II grade. 3. Stand up MLOPS / TRAINING INFRASTRUCTURE for proprietary IP (reward models, small specialist models, eval judges): distributed training (e.g. Ray on Kubernetes), GPU scheduling across on-prem and cloud bursting, experiment tracking and reproducibility, checkpoint-to-production deployment in hours not weeks. Explicitly NOT asked to train a frontier foundation model — that is not where this business creates value.
Competence bar (must-haves — treat as the rubric's "required level"): - 12+ years building software, with at least 4 as an engineering manager of managers. - Shipped at least one platform from 0 to meaningful scale (built, not merely maintained or inherited). - Hands-on enough to do architecture reviews and read PRs credibly (Python OR a typed language) — roughly 10% of the job, but non-negotiable. - Worked ADJACENT to ML systems (inference, data pipelines, training infra, eval). Does NOT need to be an ML researcher; the problems are classical platform engineering at data-company scale. - Can name one specific org-design or hiring decision that went badly and articulate the lesson.
Strong positive signals: data-intensive B2B background (annotation, analytics, observability, fintech data) or a hyperscaler ML-infra org; has operated a 25-75 person engineering org; has navigated a services-to-product transition.
Anti-unicorn calibration (do NOT penalize, and treat the opposite claims with suspicion): - No advanced-degree gate: what they built and shipped outweighs credentials. - No "frontier AI" requirement: absence of frontier-lab experience is NOT a competence gap for this role. - Distrust "full-stack hands-on across frontend, backend and cloud-native" at claimed senior level — credible senior leaders have a center of gravity; claiming all three at expert depth is itself a calibration red flag.
